claims.text: Usual FUO panel: CBC w differential; ESR, CRP, procal, LDH and ferritin; liver tests; UA w microscopy; serial blood cultures (ideally b4 abx); HIV Ab, RNA and PCR; TST or IGRA.
claims.quote: In addition to specific testing, the following should usually be done: Complete blood count with differential Erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), and ferritin Liver tests Urinalysis with microscopic examination Serial blood cultures (ideally before antimicrobial therapy) HIV antibody test, RNA concentration assays, and polymerase chain reaction assay Tuberculin skin test or interferon-gamma release assay

claims.text: Older adults need eval for GCA.
claims.quote: Older adults require evaluation for giant cell arteritis; younger adults generally do not.

claims.text: ANA and rheumatoid factor to screen for rheumatologic disorders.
claims.quote: Serologic tests, such as antinuclear antibody (ANA) and rheumatoid factor (RF), are done to screen for rheumatologic disorders.

claims.text: CT of the chest, abd and pelvis for adenopathy and occult abscesses, even w.o localizing signs.
claims.quote: However, CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis should be considered to check for adenopathy and occult abscesses even when patients do not have localizing symptoms or signs.

claims.text: Echocardiography for (+) blood cultures, or murmurs or periph signs of endocarditis.
claims.quote: If blood cultures are positive or heart murmurs or peripheral signs suggest endocarditis, echocardiography is done.

claims.text: PET can help find the focus of fever.
claims.quote: Positron emission tomography (PET) may also be useful in detecting the focus of fever.

claims.text: Bx of suspicious tissue (liver, bone marrow, skin, pleura, lymph nodes, intestine, musc).
claims.quote: Biopsy may be required if an abnormality is suspected in tissue that can be biopsied (eg, liver, bone marrow, skin, pleura, lymph nodes, intestine, muscle).
